All amounts on one price basis with the rate on the matching period; convert a quoted nominal rate with the effective-rate record before use.

models.inverse_notes: A=P*i/(1-(1+i)^-n) needs i>0 and n>=1; substitution P=77217.35, i=0.05, n=10 gives A=10000.00 within rounding. At n=1, A=P*(1+i) exactly (checked: 9523.81 x 1.05 = 10000.00 within rounding). A=0 admits P=0; P=0 with i>0, n>=1 forces A=0. Solving for i needs iteration and for n a logarithm, both unsupported by the scalar grammar, so those directions are untested. The i-to-0 limit branch P=A*n is a different expression, never a guard relaxation.
limitations: Beginning-of-period (annuity-due) streams need the distinct due factor with the extra (1+i) multiple and are not covered.
Excludes growing, variable, life-contingent, and indexed withdrawal streams; mortality and longevity risk are out of scope.

references.method: Published-table oracle: AccountingTools factor 7.7217 (n=10, 5%) x $10,000 = $77,217; the expression evaluates 77217.35 (unrounded factor 7.72173) and tolerance 0.5 covers the table's 4-decimal rounding (at most 0.00005 x 10000). Labeled cross-record recomputation on the same value: uniform-present-value@source-3 on matched inputs (annual=10000, rate=0.05, years=10) returns the identical 77217.35 -- a numerical cross-check, never an equivalence claim.

references.method: Due-PV closure recomputation: the admitted due record returns R*((1-(1+i)^-n)/i)*(1+i) = 60790.58 on matched inputs (R=5000, i=0.06, n=20); dividing by (1+i) = 1.06 per the sourced due/immediate relation reproduces this record's 57349.61. The same matched inputs through uniform-present-value@source-3 (annual=5000, rate=0.06, years=20) return the identical value. Both are labeled cross-record recomputation, never equivalence.

relationship.locator: Timing of payments; Valuation > Annuity-certain > Annuity-immediate (present-value factor, proof, PV example); Annuity-due (due-factor relation); Amortization calculations.
relationship.original_equation: P = A x [1 - (1+i)^-n] / i (present value of an ordinary annuity / annuity-immediate)
relationship.translation_notes: Direct transcription with retirement-series symbols A (level withdrawal), i (rate per period), n (withdrawal count); the factor form mirrors the admitted due-PV exponent shape (1+i)**(-n) minus the due (1+i) multiple. Dimensional check: USD times a dimensionless factor stays USD. Guards A>=0, i>0, n>=1 mirror the admitted OAFV guard shape; i>0 with n>=1 keeps the factor positive. The i=0 limit branch P=A*n is a separate expression per the OAFV precedent, never a guard relaxation. The UMD Equal-Payment-Series Present-Worth Factor P = A*([1+i]^n-1)/(i[1+i]^n) is the same mathematics in multiplied-out form.

sources.evidence: Annuity-immediate (ordinary annuity) pays at the end of each period; its unit-payment present-value factor is a-angle-n = (1-(1+i)^-n)/i with PV = R x factor; the due factor is (1+i) times the immediate factor; the loan-amortization section restates P = R*(1-(1+i)^-N)/i.
